अरुण गोविल के इस खुलासे ने मचा दिया है बॉलीवुड में तहलका! 😲
रामायण में भगवान राम का किरदार निभाने वाले अरुण गोविल ने हाल ही में एक इंटरव्यू में बताया है कि वे फिल्म Lav Kush में लक्ष्मण का रोल कभी नहीं करना चाहते थे।
उनका कहना था कि राम का यादगार किरदार निभाने के बाद लक्ष्मण बनना सही नहीं है, उन्होंने प्रोड्यूसर को मना भी किया था लेकिन किसी ने उनकी एक नहीं सुनी।
अरुण गोविल का दावा है कि गलत कास्टिंग की वजह से ही 25 जुलाई 1997 को रिलीज हुई यह फिल्म एक दिन भी नहीं चल पाई और बॉक्स ऑफिस पर डिजास्टर साबित हुई।
Devyank Arts के बैनर तले दिलीप कनिकारिया द्वारा प्रोड्यूस और V. Madhusudhana Rao द्वारा डायरेक्ट की गई इस फिल्म में जितेंद्र राम, जया प्रदा सीता, दारा सिंह हनुमान और प्राण वाल्मीकि बने थे, और इसने सिर्फ 43 लाख रुपये की कमाई की थी।
आज भी लोग उन्हें अरुण गोविल की बजाय रामजी ही मानते हैं और मेरठ निर्वाचन क्षेत्र के सांसद होने के नाते राजनीति में भी लोग यही मानकर उनके पास आते हैं कि उनका काम पक्का हो जाएगा।
क्या आपको लगता है कि किसी एक्टर का एक ही छवि में बंध जाना सही है? 🎬

ctx.title: Arun Govil says he was pressured to play Lakshman to Jeetendra's Ram in Lav Kush against his wishes, recalls film 'didn't even run for one day'
ctx.summary: After playing Lord Rama in Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan and Uttar Ramayan, Arun Govil played Lakshman in Lav Kush, a 1997 film.
ctx.text:
To a generation, Arun Govil is the personification of Lord Rama . The actor played Rama in Ramanand Sagar’s seminal TV show Ramayan, which aired from 1987-88. The show made Arun a household name, forever linking him to the image of Lord Rama. Even as the actor tried to diversify, typecasting brought him back to the mythological fold. The best example of this is the 1997 film Lav Kush, in which he played Lakshman.
In a recent interview, the veteran actor revealed that he never wanted to do the film, as he didn’t feel right about playing Lakshman, having previously done a memorable job as Lord Rama. In fact, Arun believes that ineffective casting was one of the reasons the film flopped.
“In the film Lav Kush, where Jeetendra played Rama, they wanted me as Lakshman. I had told the producer it's not right; don't make me play the character of Lakshman, but they did not listen. They wanted me. I said, ‘Okay, let's do it.’ But then, look what happened. The film didn't even run for one day. Nobody knows about that film,” Arun Govil told Variety India in an interview.
Produced by Dilip Kanikaria under the Devyank Arts banner and directed by V. Madhusudhana Rao, Lav Kush starred Jeetendra as Lord Rama, Jaya Prada as Sita, Arun Govil as Lakshman, Dara Singh as Hanuman and Pran as Valmiki. Mounted on a massive budget, the film released on 25 July 1997 and proved to be a box-office disaster, earning only ₹ 43 lakh.
Arun Govil believes that most fans see Lord Rama in him due to Ramayan’s enduring success. “Even today, people see me as Lord Rama. They even call me Ramji. They don't call me Arun Govil. Even today, in my constituency (he is a Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha, representing the Meerut constituency), all the people address me as Ramji. And they also come with the thought: ‘You are Ramji, you tell us what to do.’ Even in the political field, whoever I meet, they believe, ‘We have come to you, now our work will get done’,” the actor added.
The veteran actor returned to the world of Valmiki’s Ramayan for a third time this year as he appeared as King Dashrath, Lord Rama’s father, in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana . The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Ramayana Part One is running in theatres and has minted over ₹ 600 crore worldwide in just five days.

He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Film Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day.
